physiology:
The seat of this code is the colon, the long quiet chamber where the body does its last sorting. What stays. What goes. What gets one more chance to be useful before it's released. It is the body's boundary organ in the most literal sense, a wall with a door in it, and the wall is doing work whether or not anyone notices.

The shadow has its floor here. When the structures of a life get held too tightly, when nothing new is allowed in and nothing finished is allowed to leave, the colon is where the body registers it. A heaviness low in the belly. A holding that does not know it is holding. The mind's closed loop has a bodily mirror, and the mirror is here, in the slowest part of the gut, the part that needs time and water and dark to do what it does.

The climb out is also bodily. Things move again. Weight comes off without anyone naming it. A morning when the body simply lets something go, and the day feels lighter for reasons that have nothing to do with thinking. Realism is felt as much as understood, and one of the places it is felt is here. The wall remembers it has a door. The door opens when it is supposed to. Nothing has to be forced.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to isoleucine, an amino acid the body cannot make and must take in from food. It belongs to the small branched-chain group, named for the side-arm that gives it its shape, and the body uses it inside muscle and inside the steady regulation of blood sugar. Energy, held and released. Levels kept inside their banks.

There is a teaching folded into that. The very code of Limitation is built on a molecule whose whole job is keeping a level inside its proper range. Not too high. Not too low. The chemistry is doing in miniature what the card is teaching at every other layer: structure as a means of keeping the energy alive, not as a cage.

And isoleucine, like the others the body cannot make for itself, has to come in from outside. Even the chemistry of holding the form is not self-made. It is received, broken down, put to work. The boundary is fed before it can hold anything at all.
